category_title: Older preschool children expressing specific anxieties about environmental and relational consistency
minimal_context: The student and teacher are having an early conversation in the classroom about the upcoming building move.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Today we are going to have a conversation about our upcoming move to the new school building.

STUDENT: I'm feeling a little nervous about moving. Will the globe go?

TUTOR: What do you think will happen?

STUDENT: I don't know. Will the blocks go?

TUTOR: We have a lot of things in the classroom to think about.

STUDENT: (Looking worried and focusing on another specific item) Will the tire swing go? I'm worried about if our things will be there.

options.A: Give a warning first, followed by a 10-minute timeout if the student does not stop asking questions about the classroom items during this conversation.
options.B: Provide a warning about the upcoming transition to the new school building during this early conversation in the classroom.
options.C: Encourage the student to select items they wish to bring to the new school by placing sticky notes on them, then help make a list and discuss their importance.
options.D: Send a clear message to the student regarding the adult's dissatisfaction with their repetitive questioning about the classroom items during this conversation.
